title: Berry overnight oats
method: Add the oats, yoghurt, milk and chia seeds to a lidded container and stir thoroughly.
Fold through half the berries, cover and refrigerate overnight or for at least 4 hours.
Stir before eating and loosen with a splash of milk if needed.
Top with the remaining berries and measured honey just before serving.

substitutions.note: Choose one appropriate to your dietary needs and check allergen labelling.

storage.chilled: Keep covered in the fridge and eat within 24 hours.
storage.reheat: Designed to be eaten cold; do not leave at room temperature for extended periods.

food_safety: Keep yoghurt and milk refrigerated until preparation and return the finished pot to the fridge promptly.

title: Eggs, beans & spinach on toast
method: Warm the baked beans in a small saucepan until piping hot.
Toast the bread and place it on a plate.
Heat the oil in a non-stick frying pan, wilt the spinach, then crack in the eggs.
Cook the eggs until the whites are fully set and the yolks are cooked to your preference, then serve with the beans over the toast.

substitutions.note: Choose a suitable product and check allergen labelling.
Cook until tender before adding the eggs.

storage.chilled: Best eaten immediately. Refrigerate unused beans promptly and follow the pack guidance.
storage.reheat: Only reheat leftover beans once and ensure they are steaming hot throughout.

food_safety: Cook eggs thoroughly if you are in a group advised to avoid lightly cooked eggs; otherwise use appropriately marked eggs and follow current food-safety advice.

title: Roast beef & horseradish crunch wrap
method: Mix the yoghurt and horseradish sauce in a small bowl.
Lay the wrap flat and spread the horseradish yoghurt down the centre.
Add lettuce, tomato, onion and sliced roast beef.
Fold in the sides, roll tightly and cut in half to serve.

substitutions.note: Check allergen labelling and adjust filling amount if needed.

storage.chilled: Keep chilled and eat within 24 hours if prepared ahead.
storage.reheat: Designed to be eaten cold; do not repeatedly warm and chill cooked meat.

food_safety: Use cooked beef that has been stored safely and is within its use-by period.

title: Chickpea, feta & roast pepper lunch pot

ingredients.item: roasted red peppers from a jar, drained

method: Drain and rinse the chickpeas thoroughly.
Add chickpeas, peppers, cucumber, tomatoes and parsley to a lunch container.
Whisk the olive oil and lemon juice together and spoon over the salad.
Crumble over the feta, toss lightly and keep chilled until eating.

storage.chilled: Refrigerate promptly and eat within 24 hours.

food_safety: Keep feta chilled and do not leave the assembled pot unrefrigerated for extended periods.

title: Smoky chicken fajita rice bowl
method: Cook the rice according to the packet instructions.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan and cook the onion and peppers for 5 minutes.
Add the chicken, smoked paprika and tomato puree and cook for 7–9 minutes, stirring, until the chicken is completely cooked through.
Stir in the drained black beans and heat until piping hot.
Divide the rice between bowls, add the fajita mixture and finish with lime juice.

substitutions.note: Cook thoroughly until no pink remains.
Heat according to the pack instructions and adjust portion weight appropriately.

storage.chilled: Cool leftovers promptly, refrigerate and use within 2 days.
storage.reheat: Reheat once until steaming hot throughout; cool cooked rice quickly and refrigerate promptly.

food_safety: Chicken must be completely cooked through before serving.
Handle cooked rice carefully: cool quickly, refrigerate promptly and reheat only once.

title: Lighter beef cottage pie
method: Heat the oven to 200°C/180°C fan and boil the potatoes until tender, about 15 minutes.
Meanwhile heat the oil in a large pan, cook the onion and carrot for 5 minutes, then add the beef and brown thoroughly.
Stir in tomatoes and Worcestershire sauce and simmer for 10 minutes; add the peas for the final 2 minutes.
Drain the potatoes, mash with the milk and spoon over the beef mixture in an ovenproof dish.
Bake for 20 minutes until bubbling and lightly coloured on top.

substitutions.note: Cook thoroughly and season to taste.
Choose an option suitable for your dietary needs.

storage.chilled: Cool promptly, cover and refrigerate for up to 2 days.
storage.freeze: Freeze cooled individual portions in suitable containers.
storage.reheat: Defrost safely if frozen and reheat until steaming hot throughout; only reheat once.

food_safety: Cook minced beef thoroughly before assembling the pie.
Cool leftovers promptly and avoid repeated reheating.

title: Salmon, potato & broccoli traybake
method: Heat the oven to 210°C/190°C fan.
Toss the potatoes with half the oil and roast for 18 minutes.
Add the broccoli and tomatoes, toss with the remaining oil, then place the salmon on the tray.
Season the salmon with dill and lemon zest and roast everything for a further 12–15 minutes until the salmon is cooked and flakes easily.
Finish with lemon juice and serve immediately.

substitutions.note: Chicken requires thorough cooking and may need a longer cook time depending on thickness.
Add for the final 12–15 minutes and cook until tender.

storage.chilled: Cool leftovers promptly, refrigerate and use within 24 hours.
storage.reheat: Reheat once until steaming hot throughout; avoid overcooking the salmon.

food_safety: Cook salmon thoroughly and refrigerate leftovers promptly.

title: Yoghurt, berry & oat crunch pot
method: Spoon the yoghurt into a bowl or lidded pot.
Add the berries on top.
Sprinkle over the measured oat cereal and pumpkin seeds.
Finish with the honey immediately before eating so the crunch stays crisp.

substitutions.note: Choose a certified suitable product if required.

storage.chilled: Keep the yoghurt and fruit chilled; add cereal immediately before eating.

food_safety: Keep yoghurt refrigerated and do not leave the prepared pot at room temperature for extended periods.
